title: crossblock-cast-coalescer - minimize dequant overhead for mixed-precision streaming
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Dequantization (INT8/FP8 -> FP32) and re-quantization steps during streaming prefill and decode add measurable CPU/GPU memory-copy costs and inhibit kernel fusion across block boundaries. This ticket implements a cross-block cast coalescer that reduces redundant casts by coalescing adjacent block-level precision transitions and exposing a lightweight in-kernel casting mode to the execution planner. Goal: reduce end-to-end token latency for mixed-precision decode by 8-20% on typical webapp QPS, and reduce memory traffic during bursty prefill by ~25% for long-context models.
acceptance_criteria: New kernel interface that supports 'coalesced-cast' annotation and in-register accumulation for int8->fp16/float accumulation paths is merged to runtime main
End-to-end median decode latency reduction >= 8% on our 8xA100 perf benchmark with standard prompt mix
No regression (>1%) in log-perplexity for our eval prompt suites when using mixed-precision coalescing compared to baseline mixed-precision path
Telemetry: cast events and bytes moved emitted under 'quant.coalesce' metric; rollout flag to toggle per-customer
Automated regression tests covering single-block, cross-block, and multihead scenarios added to CI (unit + integration harness)
design_notes: High-level approach: introduce a planner pass after operator selection that detects adjacent operators with matching logical precision boundaries and rewrites the plan to insert a single coalesced-cast op instead of multiple casts

Kernel change: small API extension to allow a kernel to accept 'cast-shim' descriptors that reference an upstream buffer in its native quantized layout and perform a single fused cast+compute path (avoids roundtrip to FP32 storage)
Prefill scheduling: augment prefill/kv capture to group slices by precision domain so coalesced casts can be applied at slice flush time rather than per-layer

Trade-offs: additional planner complexity and slight increase in kernel interface surface. Risk of increased register pressure for some kernels (mitigated by a conservative register-use heuristic that falls back to per-layer casts when pressure > threshold)
Fallbacks: rollout uses per-customer config and runtime fallback to non-coalesced path for layers with dynamic shapes or where the heuristic fails
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 3d): prototype planner pass and a reference CPU-backed coalesced-cast operator in runtime-evict branch
Phase 2 (kernel work, 6d): add minimal in-kernel shim for GEMM kernels to accept cast-shim descriptor; add unit tests for correctness across INT8/FP8/FP16 flows
Phase 3 (prefill integration, 4d): update prefill scheduler to emit precision-domain flush points and annotate KV writes
Phase 4 (telemetry + rollout, 2d): add metrics (quant.coalesce.count, quant.coalesce.bytes, quant.coalesce.fallbacks) and feature-flag gated release; enable canary on Dedicated cluster
Phase 5 (perf tuning, 5d): iterate on register heuristic and microbenchmarks on A100/H100/AMD profiles
test_plan: Unit tests: numeric parity across cast paths for a representative set of matrices (shapes + strides)
Integration: end-to-end prefill + decode harness comparing baseline mixed-precision vs coalesced-cast on long-context prompts
Performance: A/B perf workloads in staging with production-like QPS to validate latency tail improvements and memory throughput reductions
Accuracy/regression: run existing eval suite to ensure no loss of quality beyond established thresholds
rollout_plan: Canary on Dedicated nodes with non-sensitive datasets for 48h
If stable, widen to 10% of hosted traffic and monitor 'quant.coalesce.fallbacks' and latency P99/P50
Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics or earlier if goals met
notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/CrossBlock+Cast+Coalescer. Prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/feature/coalesce-cast-spike. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123
